thread:
Maya: Quick heads-up — ran A/B for quant-nf4-v3 on 10% traffic earlier today. Latency p95 down ~20%, cost per 1k tokens ~-28%. However eval_chat_score dropped 1.9% and hallucination_rate on safety_eval up +0.8%. Posting short summary below, want opinions on automatic fallback thresholds / circuit-breaker rules.
canary-bot: Canary summary: https://redwood.internal/canary/2060456789  
- traffic: 10% (prod route: /generate)
- latency_p95: base=420ms -> candidate=336ms (-20%)
- cost/1k: base=$0.48 -> candidate=$0.346 (-27.9%)
- eval_chat_score (primary): base=0.862 -> cand=0.846 (delta -1.86%)
- hallucination_rate (safety_eval): base=0.42% -> cand=1.22% (delta +0.80% absolute)
- sample logs: short_incoherent_responses x9 / 1000 reqs

Vlad: 1.86% is close to our soft gate of 2%. But hallucination +0.8% absolute feels high for the /generate route (user-facing open chat). Do we treat hallucination absolute deltas as hard fails?

Sam: I think we should use a combined cost-quality tradeoff rather than raw thresholds only. Suggest a scoring heuristic: 
```
combined_score = quality_delta (%) - lambda * cost_savings (%) - mu * latency_improve (%)
# promote if combined_score >= -0.5
```
Where quality_delta is negative for regressions. Set lambda around 0.6 for prod routes, mu 0.2. This lets us tolerate tiny quality drops if cost/latency wins are big enough.

Rachel: For safety signals I'm more conservative: hallucination absolute delta >0.5% should be a hard stop for prod promotion on public routes. For internal or low-risk routes we can allow up to 1.0% with human review. Also require persistence: must be observed for >=15m sliding window or 2 consecutive evaluation batches.

Maya: Good call. Candidate is over the 0.5% hallucination hard stop. My plan: abort automatic 100% promote, run extended shadow for 2h + targeted eval set with longer context. If shadow shows hallucination <=0.5% and chat_score loss <1.2% I will bump to 30% canary and re-evaluate.

Vlad: Add hysteresis to the rollout policy: require two consecutive 5-min windows meeting thresholds before traffic increase, and require two consecutive failing windows to trigger auto-fallback. Also include cooldown: if auto-fallback occurs, lock promotion for 24h unless manually overridden.

Sam: Also propose a route-level sensitivity tag. Example: routes labeled sensitive=[user-facing-chat, billing, legal] use stricter params: quality_drop_threshold=0.5%, halluc_stop=0.3%. Non-sensitive routes use laxer thresholds. This prevents one-size-fits-all mistakes.

Rachel: We should codify the policy as JSON so automation can use it. Draft (WIP):
```
{
  "policy_name": "quant-promote-v3",
  "sensitivity":"user-facing-chat",
  "min_shadow_duration_mins": 120,
  "canary_steps": [10,30,60],
  "quality_delta_hard_stop_pct": 0.5,
  "hallucination_hard_stop_abs_pct": 0.5,
  "combined_score_thresh": -0.5,
  "consecutive_windows_req": 2,
  "window_mins": 5,
  "cooldown_hours": 24,
  "fallback_action": "switch-to:base-v2"
}
```
canary-bot: Note: current run already flagged hallucination >0.5% for 18 mins within last hour, triggering investigatory alert.

deploy-bot: Promotion job for quant-nf4-v3 -> queued? :eyes: (blocked by policy)

Maya: Action items: 1) I'll run extended shadow + longer eval set (me) 2) @Vlad will add the hysteresis + cooldown into rollout service (Vlad) 3) @Sam will prototype combined_score metric in the eval pipeline (Sam) 4) Rachel please sign off on safety threshold once we have extended eval results. If extended shadow passes I'll open a manual partial promote to 30% and post back.

Vlad: Sounds good. Also recommend adding a realtime alert rule: if hallucination_rate delta >0.3% AND sample incoherent_responses > X in 10m then page oncall with severity P2.

Sam: Fine by me. I'll mock up the metric and a notebook for the tradeoff sweep so PMs can see cost vs quality frontier.

Rachel: Thanks — will be on standby for review. :thumbsup:

Maya: Thanks team. I'll update the thread with extended-shadow link when ready.
